6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed employee bathroom in the kitchen to lack paper towels. Ensure paper towels are at each hand washing sink. Discussed with PIC. Replaced with new paper towels. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed sanitization bucket in the kitchen to be low - 0 ppm. Bleach was added - 50 to 100 ppm. PIC tested with his own test strips. Discussed with PIC that sanitization buckets should be changed every 4-6 hours or sooner dependent on weakened concentration. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed no thermometers in the front cooler (bar prep cooler and reach-in cooler). Provide thermometers for these coolers before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the baffles to have an accumulation of grease debris. Steam Power currently comes twice a year. Suggested to PIC that company comes 3x yearly due to build-up presence. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/15/21.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Provided copy with PIC. Discussed need for all food handling employees (every staff member at facility) to sign the document and understand the contents. Explained document to PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 5/25/21.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy. Provided copy to PIC. Discussed procedure with PIC. Facility has bleach to perform procedure. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed can opener blade to not be clean to sight or touch. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC - wash, rinse, and sanitize. Can opener was taken away for cleaning. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/10/20.

Observed ice scoop at server station to be placed on top of ice machine. Place ice scoop on a surface that can be washed, rinsed, and sanitized along with ice scoop. Discussed changing practice with PIC. Ice scoop was taken for wash, rinse, and sanitizing. COS.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

(REPEAT) Observed egg drop soup to be 126 degrees F - probed after mixing soup. Temperature was 87 degrees F before stirring. Time/Temperature Control for Food Safety not maintained at 135 degrees F or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements with PIC. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to 165 degrees F or above. Soup was prepared within the hour per PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/10/20.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

Observed two unlabeled spray bottles. PIC labeled each bottle upon request. Spray cleaner and alcohol were in bottles. Label with common name of material. COS.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

(REPEAT) Observed method of cooking to be inadequate - time is not documented for cooling. Discussed HACCP concept with PIC. Add time to foods that are cooling - soups, chicken placed in ice bath. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/10/20.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. 

Observed no probe thermometer at facility. Purchase a probe thermometer to measure the temperature of foods. Calibrate as needed. Inspector will follow-up on 5/25/21.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

Observed multiple areas where food items were not at least 6 inches off the floor - walk-in freezer boxes, sugar bags, boxes with canned food, rice bags, dried chili bags. Ensure all food items are at least 6 inches off the floor throughout facility.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple in-use rags at bar and throughout kitchen to not be immersed in sanitizer. Wet rags were on countertops. Discussed need for a sanitizer bucket with appropriate concentration and in-use rags held within sanitizer at all times - change sanitizer as needed when concentration runs low. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/10/20.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple areas throughout facility to have plates and bowls not inverted - no protection from cross contamination. Flip plates and bowls in order to have the food- and lip-contact surfaces covered and free from cross contamination. Observed two bowls of spoons at the bar area where spoons had food- and lip-contact surfaces mixed with spoons that handles were upright. Keep all spoons in bowl with handles upright - prevention from cross contamination. Discussed with PIC. Cease practices.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no sanitization buckets throughout facility. In-use rags were on counters with no form of sanitization buckets. Facility must have multiple sanitization buckets provided and available during all hours of operation. Ensure employee's are frequently making sanitization buckets and changing as needed. Keep in-use rags in buckets at all times. Use test strips to maintain concentration accuracy. Inspector will follow-up on 5/25/21.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following areas that were dusty or had dirt and debris:
1. Walk-in freezer fans - dust accumulation
2. Tin foil around rice steamer - change foil frequently
3. Hood baffles covered with grime and debris
4. Warmers in front of prep coolers - dust under warmers on grates
5. Walk-in cooler fans - dust accumulation

Ensure routine cleaning of facility - wash, rinse, and sanitize the above areas before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas no longer smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Caulk at 3 compartment sink of bar - moldy - re-caulk between wall and 3 compartment sink at bar
2. Caulk at dish machine area - missing on right hand side between dish machine and wall; left hand side has moldy caulk - re-caulk between dish machine and wall

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs are conducted before next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handlers licenses available during inspection. Discussed need for all employees who are NOT certified food protection manager's (CFPM's) to have food handlers licenses. Keep copies of licenses at facility in folder or binder. Ensure all employees have licensure before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed certified food protection manager's (CFPM's) to lack allergen training certification. Discussed with PIC. All CFPM's need allergen training and proof of certification. Keep copies at the facility in folder or binder. Provided copy of allergen training information. Ensure CFPM's have completed training and printed certifications before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15  (Pf) Two cans of bamboo shoots are dented and in poor condition. Food packaging must be in good condition so that foods are not exposed to adulteration or potential contamination. Reference 3-202.15. Cans were discarded. Can condition was discussed with the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Can opener blade is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A). Maintain the can opener clean and sanitized. The can opener was immediately cleaned.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Hot sour soup on the stove top is 128°F when stirred. Temperature on top was 89°F before stirring.  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to above 165°F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).  Employee was coached concerning the need to stir items that are being hot held.  Soup did not reach 165F  before it was turned back off and held at 127F. The soup was discarded.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (C) The method of cooling is inadequate in that time is not documented for cooling. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15. The will add time to foods that are cooling.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination in the walk in freezer. Observed a chunk of chicken to be frozen and uncovered in the walk in freezer. Food shall be protected at all times from contamination. Reference 3-307.11. Store food in food safe container or wrap of some sort.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. Buckets of sanitizer in the kitchen but wet wiping cloths are observed on counter tops.  Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer when not in use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf)  Observed food contact surfaces to be soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A). Observed sauce bottle in bar area to be soiled on the dispensing nozzle. Observed can opener to be soiled on the blade. Items were cleaned immediately.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Curry sauce is 55°F. Sauce was left out during lunch serving time. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and 
(B). Chicken for is observed to be on the counter at 57°F. This item is often cooked and then not cooled completely or cooled and then taken out to sit on the counter during lunch service. Discussed which way they wanted to handle this item with Elliot. The chicken will be cooked and properly cooled. Portions will be taken from cold holding as needed for this dish. This time the chicken was allowed to be kept until 6pm for service. From this point on it will be discarded if held on the counter out of temperature.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-501.112  (C) Observed, dead, mouse in the soda closet ceiling. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate mice, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.112. The mouse was removed.  The facility has regular pest control.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed a bag of carrots and a box of cauliflower on the floor in the walk in cooler. Also observed a fly strip to be hanging over the long skinny prep table in back where sauce is being placed into containers. The fly strip is empty and was removed. Discussed proper placement of such insect control devices.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location. Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the order machines which is trapped by plastic wrap. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-304.11  (C) Excessive [heat / vapors / obnoxious odors / smoke / fumes] were found in the facility. A mechanical ventilation system of sufficient capacity shall be provided to keep rooms free of excessive heat, steam, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes. Reference 6-304.11. Obnoxious odor is evident in the facility.  Have the ventilation systems evaluated for proper function and repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11. Observed an employee phone to be sitting on a prep table. The phone was moved before anything could be said. Violation was immediately corrected.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-202.12  (Pf) Hot water at employee hand sink in employee restroom is below 100F at the hand sink. Provide water of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. Reference 5-202.12.  Provide hot water in 10 days.
6-301.11  (Pf) Liquid hand soap not provided at the hand washing sink at the smoothie bar. Soap was provided at smoothie hand washing sink. Reference 6-301.11.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14  (C) A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. Provide a clearly visible handwashing sign at each hand sink. Reference 6-301.14. Signs were provided. Please post signs.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16  (P) Observed the following foods out of temperature: Beef at 47F (piled too high in the prep top) scallops at 45F in bowl on top of prep top cold holding, crab sticks at 46F in bowl on top of prep top cold holding.  Chicken on counter top at 60F during lunch. Moved to ice and remained at 64F. Chicken was and was disard.  Do not put foods in bowls on top of the inside of prep top. Do not hold food at room temperature without a time as a control policy. Garlic in oil mixture observed to be held at room temperature is 60F and was discarded. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employees and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F in reach in cooler or discarded.  Reference 3-501.16.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location on the floor in the kitchen. Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11. Put food away as soon as it is delivered. The foods were moved to proper storage.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Clean Equipment/Utensils/Linens/Single-Use Articles stored incorrectly in that a tub of dirty water for soaking soiled utensils is over clean pots and pans. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D). Proper area for soaking utensils was discussed and the soaking container was removed. Correct this process.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Walls in the dish area and the prep area are found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11. Repair the walls in these areas. Areas were shown to the owner and FSSM on duty.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 - Food managers do not have allergen training. Information was provided to manager to ensure that all food managers take the Allergen training certification.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.130 - Bulk powder storage bins were not labeled as to the contents. Provide proper labels on bulk storage bins.

Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the original packaging must be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.120 - Open jar of beef flavor paste in the bottom of the prep cooler nearest the back door had a temperature of 84F. The label on the jar states "refrigerate after opening". All other foods in the cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 37F-43F. Product was stored on a table by the wok overnight and placed in the cooler upon arrival of inspector. Beef flavor paste was discarded in the trash.
Potentially hazardous foods must be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage. Products that are stored at ambient temperature but require refrigeration after opening must be chilled to a temperature of 41F/below w/in 4hrs after opening and held in a cooler at 41F/below during storage.

750.151 - Rangoon filling, open gallon of milk, sliced melon, and cut tofu were observed without date marks. Other foods prepared on 9/5 were dated 9/6. Proper dating of ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods was discussed. Benefit of doubt was given; foods were labeled with dates and kept for use. 
Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly labeled with date of prep/opening and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
findings.citation_text:
750.153 - Tub of par-fried chicken pulled from the walkin cooler upon arrival of staff was observed on the cook line. The tub was not labeled with the time. Surface temperatures were observed at 52F-60F. Chicken in the bottom of the tub had an internal temperatures of 40F. Per manager's request, staff labeled the pan with the time to indicate when food needed to be discarded.
When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when it was removed from a temperature controlled environment and/or when it is to be discarded. Properly label food foods and discard after 4hrs.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 130 - (R) A) Several foods were observed uncovered, including but not necessarily limited to, dry noodles and a plastic container of flour left out on a metal cart on the cook line overnight and pans of foods in the prep coolers. All foods must be covered between uses and during overnight storage.

B) Pan of food was observed on the floor under shelving in the walkin freezer. Store foods up off the floor at least 6 inches.

Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food. Food shall be stored in clean, covered containers once being removed from the original package.
Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - (R) Observed an old Oyster Flavored Sauce can to be used as the scoop in the bulk rice container. Pulled from use during the inspection. Cease using old cans as scoops within foods (even foods that still need to be cooked).

Food handlers & consumers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods.  When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.)

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750.280 - Scoops in bulk powder bins were soiled with general buildup from use. Clean and sanitize bulk powder scoops at the end of operations daily.
Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoop was observed on top of ice machine. Plate as provided for scoop storage.
Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handles extended out of the ice. Clean and sanitize ice scoops and storage plates/containers daily.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Inspector arrived at facility around 1020a and walked in with staff around 1045a. Employees were observed going to wok and beginning work without first washing hands. Hands were washed at request of inspector. 

Employees must properly wash hands any time hands may have been contaminated, between tasks as needed, and upon arriving at work and prior  to working with food, clean equipment and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - A) Ice cream freezer at smoothie bar was observed with heavy ice accumulation inside. Defrost the ice cream freezer.

B) The following were observed to be rusty and in need of repairs and/or replacing:
1. metal cart in dish area;  and
2. walkin cooler shelves.
Clean and re-surface the walkin cooler shelving and the metal cart of replace them.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Barely damp green towel was observed being used to wipe down a prep table and was then left on the table when employee stepped away from his current task. Container of bleach solution was in the area for use (200ppm chlorine). Staff were advised to wipe down tables and other surfaces with wiping cloths from a bleach solution and to store wiping cloths in the bleach solution between uses. Towel was placed in the bleach solution for storage/use.

Maintain bleach solutions at 100-200ppm; store wiping cloths in solutions between uses.
Moist cloths used for wiping surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
Non-food contact surfaces clean
Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Soap was not available at smoothie bar handsink. 

Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1130 - (R) Dumpster was observed open upon arrival of inspector. Dumpster had some debris and puddling liquid in the bottoms. Close the dumpster lid when not in use.

Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers and shall be kept covered when not in use.

findings.title: Outside storage area clean, enclosure properly constructed
findings.citation_text:
750.1140 - (R) Litter and trash were observed on the ground in and around the dumpster corral. Patrol the area around the dumpster and clean up litter/debris daily.

Outside storage area shall be large enough to store the outside garbage and refuse containers and shall be kept clean.
**Also, empty the bucket next to the picnic table out back used for cigarette butts and trash daily/as needed**

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 153 - Foods were left out over lunch period and then placed back in the cooler after lunch rush. Surface and internal temperatures ranged from 53F to 70F. Foods included minced garlic (60F; bottom of prep cooler), red curry sauce (53F; 2 door cooler), and par-fried egg rolls (70F; fridge by fryers). All foods were discarded in the trash. Manager was once again advised on time control versus cold holding. Foods that are not temperature controlled and are out at ambient temperature during lunch and dinner rushes must either have time tracked and be discarded at the end of lunch and dinner or must be maintained at proper temperatures (cold foods 41f/below; hot foods 135F/above). Options for tracking time were discussed.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at proper product temperature at all times during storage (41F/below, or 135F/above) unless time control is used. If time control is used for working supplies of potentially hazardous foods, then a policy must be established for tracking time to ensure foods will be used/served or discarded in 4hrs or less. Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. 
**Establish and adhere to a time control policy if time control is going to be utilized. Track time using a dry erase board, stickers, or any other method that is easy for staff to understand.**

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Raw shrimp was observed in a bucket of water by the vegetable prep sink. Staff noted the shrimp were frozen and placed in the water to thaw. The internal temperature of shrimp was observed at 55F. Shrimp were placed in walkin cooler.
**Manager was advised potentially hazardous foods must never be thawed at ambient temperature in standing water. If cold running water is used, products must be placed in a cooler or used within 2hrs or less. Planning ahead and thawing foods in the walkin cooler or another functioning cooler holding at 41F/below is the best and safest way to thaw potentially hazardous foods.**

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.130 - Pan of raw chicken breasts was observed on top of pans of raw beef and raw pork in a prep cooler on the make line. Raw foods were rearranged so raw chicken was not directly above raw beef and pork.

All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  All raw meat shall be properly stored in the order of cooking requirements. The meats that have the lowest temperature cooking requirement (seafood = 145F) must be stored above all other raw meats. Chicken has the highest temperature cooking requirement (165F) and must be stored below all other raw meats. Beef and pork may be stored on the same shelf below seafood but above chicken. Always store raw meats below and separate from ready to eat foods.

Paper towels should be ready for use and should  be used to shut off the manual faucet after hands are dried to avoid potential recontamination of freshly washed hands.
Also, gloves are only meant for one use and must be discarded when they become torn, dirty, and/or their is an interruption in task.
